title: The STE push guard reads a commit's folder from its own segment, not the call's first `git -C`
why: In one call such as `git -C <A> status && cd <B> && git commit -am m && git push`, rule ste-push takes the commit's folder from the first `-C` (command_root), so it misses B's commit, skips the chain refusal and lints B's pre-commit HEAD (lane lint-before-record-push, 04:05 CST Nov 8). Follow-up of step lint-before-record-push (#1755).
note: Fix: `_segment_top` in hooks/guard_merge.py uses dir_before_segment, as the conflict-markers check does. Red case first: that chain passes today; control: a one-folder commit and push still lints as today.
